task: A new manager asks you what stonewalling is and how to take a time-out instead. Explain it to them in two sentences.
model: Stonewalling means going quiet or withdrawing without saying why, leaving the other person feeling ignored. For a time-out, say you need a pause, agree when to resume the conversation, then return.

ideas.heading: Stonewalling
ideas.body: Stonewalling is going silent, withdrawing or changing the subject without saying why. The other person feels ignored or rejected. The problem stays unsolved.
ideas.label: Stonewalling is withdrawing without saying why.
ideas.met: You explained that stonewalling means withdrawing without saying why.
ideas.missed: Describe stonewalling: going silent, withdrawing or changing the subject without saying why.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you explained stonewalling. Describe what the person does.

ideas.heading: Taking a time-out
ideas.body: Tell the other person you need a pause. For example, "I need ten minutes to think about this." You can step away to calm down. Leaving without saying why is stonewalling.
ideas.label: You tell the other person you need a pause.
ideas.met: You said to tell the other person you need a pause.
ideas.missed: Say to tell the other person you need a pause.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you said to announce the pause.

ideas.heading: Coming back
ideas.body: Agree when you'll resume the conversation, then return. This keeps the other person from waiting without knowing when you'll be back.
ideas.label: You agree when to resume the conversation, then return.
ideas.met: You said to agree when to resume the conversation, then return.
ideas.missed: Say to agree when to resume the conversation, then return.
ideas.unsure: It's unclear whether you said to return to the conversation.
